title: Any suggestions for improvement? This might be useful for you too!
author: haze_hoppelt_imblock
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’m working on a project called **Chart Lens Studio** with the help of ChatGPT (Codex). The tool is just for my personal use, so it runs locally. I’ve connected my MacBook to a Raspberry Pi 5, which handles the data storage (1 TB).  
One of the screenshots shows how the program is set up, and the other shows what it looks like on TradingView. I had a Chrome extension built to connect the tool to TradingView.  
Maybe you have some ideas or suggestions, or maybe this could help you build something of your own. Enjoy!

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
One improvement I’d prioritize is making the Chrome extension save a small context record with every TradingView capture: symbol, exchange, timeframe, timezone, bar-close status, indicator settings, and capture time. Otherwise two charts that look similar may represent different inputs, especially if the current candle is still moving.

Since the screenshots aren’t available here, I’d check whether Chart Lens Studio already exposes that metadata and whether the Raspberry Pi 5 stores it beside the chart. Can you reopen an old capture and reconstruct the exact TradingView state that produced it?

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body:
That's a good point, and I'd add a few fields to the record. The data feed and exchange the chart is using matter, because the same symbol can show different candles from different feeds. The version of each indicator or script and its inputs should be saved too, since a script update can change old values. And a hash of the underlying candle data or the screenshot ties the record to exactly what was seen.

Your last question is the best test: pick a capture from a few weeks ago, rebuild the state from the saved record alone, and check whether the indicator values match what was on the screen. If they don't match, something is missing from the context record.

replies.author: haze_hoppelt_imblock
replies.body: 80% of that is already built in, guys, but thanks anyway!
